title: Differential Oracle test+verify capstone
description: E2.TEST capstone for the live differential oracle and the Node/Bun denominator. Drives the differential-oracle stack through the DW.STD (bd-fqlfw.11) e2e bundle harness: the capstone integration test, the operator-facing `frankenctl oracle run|report` CLI, the differential-oracle integration, the E2.T5 divergence-preserving minimizer, and the in-module unit tests. In ci/test mode it also runs a fixed, hermetic franken+core corpus through the real CLI, persisting a content-addressed oracle bundle (manifest.json + report.json + repro.lock, plus a manifest-addressed degraded_receipt.json iff degraded) and re-verifying it byte-identically with `frankenctl oracle report`.

modes.check: cargo check the frankenctl binary + the capstone and CLI test targets
modes.test: run the verification test suite (no live corpus distinction from ci)
modes.ci: run the verification test suite, then the live franken+core corpus
modes.corpus: run only the live franken+core corpus into the run dir

acceptance.content_addressed_bundle: Each corpus case emits manifest.json + report.json + repro.lock, plus degraded_receipt.json iff degraded. Emission requires a new 0700 directory beneath an existing trusted or sticky-protected parent, pins that parent before mkdir/open, uses exclusive no-follow artifact creation, and publishes the manifest last. `frankenctl oracle report` requires the exact declared artifact set, canonical source and artifact hashes, and bundle_id; reads through a pinned directory descriptor; rejects symlinks, semantic cross-file mismatches, stream-hash drift, escaping paths, or canonicalization drift; and conservatively reclassifies stored taxonomy from receipts.
acceptance.canonicalization: Number formatting, NaN, Infinity, -0, float rounding, and BigInt-boundary integers are equated across the two independent interpreters (semantic consensus); a real structured value difference is surfaced as a divergence, never smoothed away.
acceptance.divergence_taxonomy: All seven divergence classes are enumerable with stable, unique wire labels.
acceptance.taxonomy_trust_boundary: Taxonomy v2 derives specialized classes only from private typed in-process runner signals. Values, group samples, stdout, stderr, serialized diagnostics, and structural group shape are evidence-only. Intentional-security classification requires an opaque live candidate plus an explicit in-memory authority record bound to source bytes, typed base class, mode, ignored lanes, and exact hash-to-backend membership topology; the default runner never synthesizes waiver authority.
acceptance.engine_core_free_oracle: The engine<->franken-core internal twin reports every classified divergence as a defect carrying a minimized reproducer that independently re-classifies to the same divergence signature (the minimizer never over-minimizes).
acceptance.degraded_path: A requested reference runtime that is absent yields a manifest-addressed, semantically cross-checked degraded_receipt.json (FE-REPRO-0007) and a non-zero exit (4) - never a silent pass. Legacy degraded bundle-v1 manifests that omit this artifact are intentionally rejected as incomplete.
acceptance.claim: FE-CLAIM-010 (Node/Bun denominator throughput) is the honest, repro.lock-backed `target` state - a measured denominator below the >= 3x floor - and the oracle refuses to fabricate a denominator from a single lane (insufficient_data, exit 4). Simulated/mock evidence (hot_paths_simulation / MockCertificate) is absent from the linked artifact.

trust_boundary.classification_inputs: private non-serialized FrankenEngine EvalErrorCode or FrankenCore stage/interpreter-error signals plus comparison mode; absent a trusted signal the class is runtime
trust_boundary.intentional_security_authority: opaque live candidate plus explicit DifferentialWaiverAuthority bound to the SHA-256 of live source bytes, typed base class, comparison mode, ignored lanes, and exact canonical hash-to-backend membership topology; only a typed candidate spanning a real reference and internal lane is eligible
trust_boundary.default_policy: no authority; no generated waiver ids; every engine-core divergence remains a defect
trust_boundary.archive_ingestion: supported schemas only; canonicalization is recomputed and must match receipts; effective taxonomy is conservatively rebuilt without typed sidecars, so stored specialized classes and waiver ids are audit data rather than authority
trust_boundary.legacy_v1: readable for audit history and conservatively reclassified; stored auto-derived waiver ids are never taxonomy-v2 authority

classes.label: parser
classes.meaning: a trusted in-process runner signal identifies a parse-stage disagreement among comparable observations.

classes.label: lowering
classes.meaning: the lanes agree on the parse but lower the program to different executable IR shapes.

classes.label: runtime
classes.meaning: both lanes complete but produce different structured values or exception classes.

classes.label: module_resolution
classes.meaning: the lanes resolve an import/module specifier differently.

classes.label: hostcall_policy
classes.meaning: the lanes apply different capability/hostcall policy on the same edge.

classes.label: intentional_security_divergence
classes.meaning: FrankenEngine deliberately diverges from a reference runtime to enforce a security boundary; requires exact explicit authority and carries the caller-supplied waiver_id; it is NOT a defect.

classes.label: reference_runtime_bug
classes.meaning: reserved for separately authenticated reference-runtime attribution; guest-controlled backend grouping alone never assigns ownership.

bundle_contract.manifest.json: schema franken-engine.oracle-run-bundle.v1: case_id, source_sha256, semantic_verdict, divergence_count, degraded flag, selected_backends, host facts, the exact sha256-indexed artifact set (report + lock, plus degraded_receipt iff degraded), and a content-addressed bundle_id.
bundle_contract.report.json: the full DifferentialOracleReport (per-backend receipts with timing, canonicalization report, divergence taxonomy report), canonical-JSON encoded and sha256-addressed by the manifest.
bundle_contract.repro.lock: schema franken-engine.repro-lock.v1: case_id, source_sha256, selected_backends, the re-run command, and the determinism contract. The reproducible assertion is the SEMANTIC VERDICT over canonical structured values and exception classes - NOT raw wall-clock timing (allow_wall_clock=true precisely because per-backend timing is non-deterministic).
bundle_contract.degraded_receipt.json: schema franken-engine.oracle-run-degraded-receipt.v1 (only when a requested reference runtime was unavailable and always sha256-addressed by the manifest): error_code FE-REPRO-0007, the unavailable runtime(s), and the policy statement that a degraded run does not assert cross-runtime consensus.

exit_codes.0: consensus - all applicable lanes agree on the semantic verdict
exit_codes.3: divergence - a classified semantic divergence was found
exit_codes.4: insufficient-data or degraded - fewer than two applicable lanes reached a comparable verdict, or a requested reference runtime was unavailable

fe_claim_010.note: A fairness-compliant Node/Bun denominator is linked (bd-fqlfw.2.6/2.7); the native baseline interpreter does NOT meet the >= 3x floor, so the claim stays target - backed by a measured, repro.lock-addressed denominator rather than absence of data. Separately gated by scripts/run_e2_denominator_bundle_gate.sh.
